summary: At step 249, kicking a non-boulder object over an unseen web reaches dokick.c:really_kick_object(). C calls find_trap(trap), which marks the web seen, exercises wisdom, updates the remembered glyph and prints 'You find a web.' before the refusal. JavaScript already has the equivalent discovery sequence inside detect.js's private findTrap helper for explicit searching, but the kick caller records note_unported('detect.c find_trap') and skips it. Expose and reuse that source-owned behavior from both callers.

source.branch: A kicked object reaches really_kick_object() with a web (or pit) trap at the target square and the trap has not yet been seen.

evidence: C source nethack-c/upstream/src/detect.c:1935-1962 defines find_trap(): it marks trap->tseen, exercises A_WIS, calls feel_newsym(), clears and maps the trap when hallucinating or when the remembered glyph differs, prints 'You find <trap>.', and waits/redraws after the cluttered-map branch.

C caller nethack-c/upstream/src/dokick.c:521-530 calls find_trap() for an unseen pit or web before printing the cannot-kick message. The existing JavaScript js/dokick.js:653-661 instead records note_unported('detect.c find_trap'), skipping the wisdom RNG and discovery message seen at the mismatch.

C caller nethack-c/upstream/src/detect.c:2079-2088 also calls find_trap() from dosearch0(); JavaScript js/detect.js has the matching discovery behavior in its private findTrap() used by dosearch0(), so make that behavior the exported find_trap() source owner and keep the existing explicit-search caller wired through it.

Saved baseline challenges/evaluations/admission-3fc2021644e79e564fb762bc2038139c3241ff42-v64.json records 265/267 screens, 5443/5447 RNG entries, and 266/267 cursors. Its first mismatch is segment 0 step 249, key 'h': C draws rn2(19)=1 from exercise(attrib.c:509), while JavaScript reaches a later rn2(70)=27 because it skips find_trap().
